answer: An applicant earns admission only after running a public beacon at one declared network vertex for twenty-one consecutive days, emitting a signed pulse every six hours that three established operators at adjacent vertices countersign within one hour. Each countersigner locks a slashable forty-credit bond on that pulse; a missed window, or a pulse whose timing fingerprint matches another applicant, slashes those bonds and restarts the stay. A farm of N names needs N distinct vertices, continuous uptime, and 3N willing neighbors — a shared host or cloned schedule burns every bond in the cluster.
